summary: Replace the random local search with a systematic search over simplex-shaped sets {x in Z^d, x_i ≥ 0, sum x_i ≤ n}, embedded into the integers in base 4n+3. For each (d, n) with at most 4000 points it computes the true score and returns the best set.

Embed the simplex sets in base 2n+1 instead of 4n+3. This still preserves all sums and differences, and it lets the search reach larger dimensions d within the 1e15 bound, so more (d, n) candidates are scored. The loop also now has time-aware skipping.

I extended the search family from plain simplices to simplices with a per-coordinate cap (x_i ≤ c, sum ≤ n). A DP counts each candidate's size first, the sets are embedded in base 2c+1, and every candidate is scored under a time budget. I haven't run it, so I don't know whether the capped sets score

After the plain simplex search, I add a second stage that tries "slab" sets {x ≥ 0 : m ≤ sum(x) ≤ n} for larger (d, n) values, which the 4000-point limit excludes for the full simplex. Pairs are visited in order of closeness to the best plain simplex, under a time budget, and the best true score win

I keep the plain simplex search, then run simulated annealing starting from the best simplex. The annealing toggles points in the next-larger simplex, which is the universe. It uses precomputed sum/difference index tables with incremental counts, so each move costs O(N). The result is returned only

After the plain simplex search, I add a second stage over weighted simplices {x ≥ 0 : Σ w_i x_i ≤ T} with weights in {1,2,3}. These give much finer size and shape choices than integer (d, n). Candidates are ordered by closeness in size to the best plain simplex and scored exactly under a time budget

I compute the exact simplex sum and difference counts analytically for every (d, n) with at most 4000 points. Use a different approach: embed the lattice simplex {x in N^d : sum x ≤ n} into the integers in base 2n+1. Closed-form counts for |A+A| and |A-A| are used to choose the best (d, n) with at most 4000 points.
